narrative.overview:
Devpilot is an operational workspace with a quiet graphite shell and a warm, paper-like work surface. It is precise and dense without feeling compressed: one current delivery decision leads, while tables, rails, and drawers disclose deeper evidence only where it helps an operator act.

The visual system treats AI as contextual explanation, not as the application's navigation model or source of production truth. Cobalt marks deliberate action, semantic colors stay narrow, and the most important blocker or next step remains attached to the object it affects.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper workspace framed by a graphite operating shell.
One dark current-task surface before supporting evidence.
Dense information expressed through alignment, dividers, and narrow inspection panes.
Cobalt actions with icon-and-label semantic states.
Contextual AI and evidence drawers that never imply a production mutation.

rules.name: The Current Decision Rule
rules.body: Every screen identifies one decision or task before it expands into records, evidence, or history.

rules.name: The Narrow Semantics Rule
rules.body: A semantic color must be paired with an icon and a written state; color never carries the outcome alone.

rules.name: The Evidence Mono Rule
rules.body: Use monospace for machine-verifiable identifiers and comparable numerals, never as a decorative developer aesthetic.

rules.name: The Attached Action Rule
rules.body: Place repair and evidence actions beside the state they change or explain; do not separate the warning from its destination.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Floating Rule
rules.body: Use borders and tonal layering for resting surfaces; use shadow only when an object floats above the work surface or a primary action needs a restrained lift.

rules.name: The Bounded Radius Rule
rules.body: Keep operational containers between 10px and 14px, controls between 7px and 8px, and reserve full circles or pills for avatars and continuous progress geometry.

dos: Do lead with one current delivery decision and keep its action beside the cause.
Do use tables, divided lists, narrow rails, and inspection panes for dense operational evidence.
Do pair every semantic color with an icon and explicit state label.
Do reserve monospace for versions, durations, commits, manifests, ports, and run IDs.
Do keep mobile status, cause, evidence access, and primary action equivalent to desktop.
Do treat finish review, verdict, canonical documentation, and raster provenance as part of shipping.
donts: Don't turn the product into a KPI-card dashboard or a chat-first navigation surface.
Don't imply that an AI explanation or proposal changed production state.
Don't replace collections with a wall of standalone cards.
Don't use semantic color without a written state and icon.
Don't add photographic or decorative product imagery where the operational UI has no verified asset need.
Don't introduce additional shadows, radii, colors, or breakpoints without first finding an implemented source.
